stage.https.title: HTTPS
stage.capture.title: Webhook capture
stage.https.description: Optional. To work on HTTPS traffic, the forward proxy signs the sites it intercepts with a root certificate made on this computer. You can set this up later in Settings.
stage.capture.description: Optional. Capture lets a provider such as GitHub or Stripe send a real webhook to Bifurc through a temporary Cloudflare tunnel, so its payload and headers can be reused. It needs cloudflared, which is installed from its official release and checked before it is used. You can do this later in Settings.
stage.proxies.title: Proxy ports
stage.proxies.description: The ports Bifurc's two proxies listen on.
stage.workspace.title: Set up your first workspace
stage.workspace.description: A workspace holds your requests, mocks, mappings and environments.
language.row.title: Language
language.row.description: The language of every label, message and button.
preferences.theme.title: Color theme
preferences.theme.description: Each theme is light or dark.
preferences.size.title: Interface size
preferences.size.description: Scales text, spacing and controls together.
problem.server_start: The {name} could not start on port {port}: {error}.
problem.port_range: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
problem.ports_differ: The two proxies need different ports.
problem.choose_other: {problem} Choose another port, or continue and change it later in Settings.
problem.low_ports_refused: {problem} Bifurc was not allowed to use ports below {reserved}: {why}. Choose another port, or continue and change it later in Settings.
terms.body: The terms of service are the agreement between you and Bifurc: what you may use the app for, what it comes with and without, and who is responsible for what. They also say that anonymous usage analytics are on by default and can be turned off in Settings, under About. Read them before you go on.
terms.accept_label: I have read and accept the terms of service
privacy.body: Your workspaces, requests and captured traffic stay on this computer. Bifurc sends anonymous usage analytics: what kind of thing you do, from which interface and on which platform, and where in Bifurc's own code it crashed or failed. Never a name, a URL, a path or anything you typed. They are on by default once you accept, and you can turn them off at any time in Settings, under About; that Bifurc was installed on this device is still reported, once.
privacy.accept_label: I have read and accept the privacy policy
overview.requests.title: Requests
overview.requests.description: Send REST, GraphQL, gRPC, SOAP and WebSocket requests, one at a time or a folder in a run.
overview.mocks.title: Mocks
overview.mocks.description: Answer a call yourself, for an endpoint that is missing or that you want to behave differently.
overview.mappings.title: Mappings
overview.mappings.description: Give local services names: api.localhost reaches the service on port 3000.
overview.proxy_rules.title: Proxy rules and capture
overview.proxy_rules.description: Send a browser or a tool through the forward proxy to redirect, mock and record its traffic.
overview.environments.title: Environments and vaults
overview.environments.description: Keep variables for each environment, and secrets sealed behind a passphrase.
overview.workspaces.title: Workspaces
overview.workspaces.description: Everything you save is a file in a workspace with its history. Syncing it with GitHub is optional.
https.import_tooltip: Use your own certificate and private key instead
capture.title: cloudflared
capture.missing: Not installed. Capture stays off until it is.
capture.unsupported: There is no cloudflared build for this computer.
https.root.title: Root certificate
https.trust.title: Trust on this computer
https.trust.description: Adds the certificate to your trusted roots, so intercepted sites open without warnings. Firefox keeps its own store and needs the certificate imported there.
https.intercept.title: Intercept HTTPS
https.intercept.description: Decrypt HTTPS traffic through the forward proxy so rules, mocks and capture apply to it.
port.title: Port
reverse.title: Reverse proxy
reverse.description: Serves your .localhost names and sends each one on to its mapping.
reverse.port_description: Keep {port} for names that work without a port, like {plain}. On any other port, every address needs that port, like {example}.
reverse.port_note: Add :{port} to every .localhost address you open or call: {address} instead of {plain}.
reverse.port_names_need: Names need the port while the reverse proxy is on {port}
reverse.permission_note: Linux only lets a program listen below {reserved} when it has been allowed to. If Bifurc's engine is not allowed yet, continuing asks for your password to allow it; refuse, and port {port} stays closed. A port from {reserved} up, such as 8000, needs no permission.
forward.title: Forward proxy
forward.description: Point a browser or a tool at it to apply proxy rules, mocks and capture to its traffic.
forward.address_known: The proxy address to give a browser or a tool is http://localhost:{port}.
forward.address_unknown: The proxy address to give a browser or a tool uses this port.
proxies.takes_effect: A new port takes effect at once while its proxy is running.
proxies.not_started: Neither proxy has been started yet. Both start on these ports when you continue, and with Bifurc from then on.
